clue.text: Leave name on pot in specialist language

indicators.note: in an across clue one part sitting on another means it comes after it

blocks.note: a jar is a pot
to go is to leave
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a label on a pot written in technical terms only experts understand.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is read in reverse: the pot comes first, with leave and name placed on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon is the vocabulary peculiar to a trade or profession, hard for outsiders to follow.

clue.text: One imposed on, pensioner supporting US soldiers

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part sits underneath, so it is written after the other part

blocks.note: GI Joes are American soldiers
OAP is old-age pensioner

explanation.surface: An elderly person is taken advantage of while propping up American troops.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP (old-age pensioner) is a British abbreviation; Joe Soap is British slang for an ordinary person who gets put upon.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Soap is a slang name for the dupe or average man who gets landed with the dull jobs.

clue.text: Inflate article during climb

indicators.note: something happening during something else sits within it

blocks.note: the indefinite article
to rise is to climb

explanation.surface: A balloonist pumps up the envelope while gaining height.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise prices or expectations is to push them higher, as one would inflate them.

clue.text: Old boy playing violin in ignorance

indicators.note: playing an instrument suggests its letters are worked over into a new arrangement

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
the instrument's name, taken as written

explanation.surface: A former pupil fiddles away, unaware of the world around him.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivion is the state of being unaware or forgetful, which is a kind of ignorance.

clue.text: Small telescope agent put in front of good girl

indicators.note: the first part is placed before the rest in the line of letters

blocks.note: a spy is a secret agent
G is the abbreviation for good
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A secret agent with a small telescope is stationed ahead of a well-behaved girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A spyglass is a hand-held, small telescope of the kind used at sea.

clue.text: Drink, especially pleasing thing, make unknown

blocks.note: a peach is something or someone excellent
a make of product is a brand
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: A tasty drink, a real treat, whose maker remains anonymous.
explanation.definitionFit: Peach brandy is a spirit or liqueur flavoured with peaches, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Channel in front of gondola, say

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of gondola
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A Venetian gondolier calls out something in the canal ahead of the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Venetian picture makes 'Channel' look like a canal; it is a roadside drain.
explanation.definitionFit: A gutter is a channel for carrying away rainwater, along a roof or the edge of a street.

clue.text: Reptile flying at gorilla

indicators.note: letters flying about land in a different order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A reptile launches itself at a gorilla in some jungle brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: An alligator is a large crocodilian reptile found in America and China.

clue.text: Withdraw cash

blocks.note: first meaning: to pull a horse or competitor out of a race
second meaning: slang for money

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests taking money out of a bank; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To scratch a runner is to withdraw it from an event, and scratch is also informal slang for money.

clue.text: Fit to eat from deli? Be prepared!

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready, worked into a new form

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Food bought at a delicatessen can be eaten, provided you are ready, like a Scout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be prepared!' is the Scout motto, which hides the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible describes food that is safe and suitable for eating.

clue.text: Rebel, warty, let out

indicators.note: letters let out run loose and come back in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A warty insurgent has been released from prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381.
explanation.definitionFit: Wat Tyler was the leader of a famous medieval uprising, so he is a historical rebel.

clue.text: Merry individual in charge of rowers?

blocks.note: first meaning: tipsy, having drunk a little too much
second meaning, read literally: a single person set above a rowing crew of eight

explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom for being slightly drunk is taken literally: one person over a rowing eight, such as the cox.
explanation.definitionFit: Having had one over the eight is a British idiom for being a little drunk, the cheerful state called merry.

clue.text: Make waves, as the sea may?

blocks.note: first meaning: to cause trouble or disturb the status quo
second meaning, literally: what a rough sea does to a vessel

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'make waves' is set beside a sea that literally does make waves and tosses a craft.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock the boat is an idiom for upsetting a stable situation, just as making waves means stirring up trouble.

clue.text: Father to study certificate for show

indicators.note: one thing added to another is joined directly after it

blocks.note: pop is an informal word for father
to con is an old word for studying closely
cert is short for certificate

explanation.surface: Dad goes off to study for an exam certificate, ready to show it off.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop concert is a live music performance, a show given by pop musicians.

clue.text: Ruler in old marquee entertained by head

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is held inside the host's home

blocks.note: the pate is the top of the head
O is the abbreviation for old
a marquee is a large tent

explanation.surface: A monarch in a vintage marquee is being hosted by the headmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A potentate is a monarch or other ruler with great power.

clue.text: Some without a home, in a state

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a part of their letters is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word, the next, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Certain homeless people live in a particular American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: A Stuart warring close to watercourse in flood

indicators.note: a warring party is in turmoil, so the letters are thrown into disorder
the close of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of watercourse

explanation.surface: A Stuart royal at war near a river while it floods.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stuarts were a British royal house, which the surface uses to suggest civil war.
explanation.definitionFit: To saturate is to soak something completely, as a flood of water would.

clue.text: Little woman in punt with husband

indicators.note: with means accompanied by, so one part is placed beside the other

blocks.note: a punt is a bet, as in a flutter on a horse
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A petite woman sits in a flat river boat alongside her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punt' suggests a boat; here it is a gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: Beth March is one of the four sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women.

clue.text: Reportedly noisy golf club

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than read, so the word goes by its sound

blocks.note: brassy means loud and harsh, like brass instruments

explanation.surface: People say there is a rowdy golf club in the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golf club' suggests the members' clubhouse; it is the stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassie is an old name for a wooden golf club, the two-wood, with a brass sole plate.

clue.text: A tall nurse treated comic actor

indicators.note: something treated has been worked on and altered from its first state

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tall nurse gave medical care to a comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: Stan Laurel was the thin half of the comedy double act Laurel and Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan Laurel was a film comedian, the English-born partner of Oliver Hardy.

clue.text: All in on processing a wool extract

indicators.note: processing works raw material into a new shape

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Everyone joins in treating fleece to get something out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanolin is the greasy substance obtained from sheep's wool, used in ointments and cosmetics.

clue.text: Not as busy in class?

blocks.note: less is the opposite of more
on means happening or occupied, as in having a lot on

explanation.surface: Is it quieter during school time?
explanation.walkthrough: Having less on means being not so busy, so the phrase splits into its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is a period of teaching, the same thing as a class in school.

clue.text: Potentially great, one guy in a French film

indicators.note: potentially means could become, so the letters may turn into something else

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
un is French for a

explanation.surface: A man who could become great stars in a French movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie Get Your Gun is a 1950 Hollywood musical film about the sharpshooter Annie Oakley.

clue.text: Father eating last on menu, a Dutch cheese

indicators.note: what is eaten ends up inside the eater
the last letter of the following word is the one kept

blocks.note: God the Father
the final letter of menu
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dad tucks into the final item on the menu, a cheese from Holland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' suggests a dad or priest; here it is God, holding one letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouda is a mild yellow cheese named after a town in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Crack marksman still

blocks.note: to crack is to snap
a good shot is a skilled marksman

explanation.surface: An expert sniper remains motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' reads as an adverb or adjective; it is the noun for a single photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is an informal photograph, and a still is a single photographic image.

clue.text: Guide by hand

blocks.note: first meaning: a handbook of instructions
second meaning: done with the hands rather than by machine

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests leading someone by the hand; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A manual is a handbook giving instructions, and manual work is done by hand rather than by machine.

clue.text: Forever in entirety, possibly

definitions.note: used as a noun, as in 'it took forever'

indicators.note: possibly signals one arrangement among the many that could be made

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Perhaps something lasts for all time in its whole extent.
explanation.definitionFit: An eternity is endless time, or informally a very long wait, which is what 'forever' names when used as a noun.

clue.text: Keep terriers in check

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: the Territorial Army, whose part-time soldiers are nicknamed terriers
to rein in is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: An owner holds back unruly dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: The terriers are not dogs: TA is Britain's Territorial Army, the volunteer reserve, whose members are called terriers.
explanation.definitionFit: To retain something is to continue possessing it rather than giving it up, a direct synonym.
